target: Nid aur yw popeth melyn, yn ôl y dihareb.
english: Not everything yellow is gold, according to the proverb.
tip: 'yn ôl' means both 'back', as in 'mynd yn ôl', and 'according to': 'yn ôl y dihareb' = according to the proverb.

target: Gwell hwyr na hwyrach.
english: Better late than never.
tip: 'gwell' (better) is the irregular comparative of 'da' (good). You never say 'da-ach'. Pair it with 'na' (than).

target: Bwytais i frecwast cynnar.
english: I ate an early breakfast.
tip: A direct object soft-mutates after a short-form verb: 'brecwast' becomes 'frecwast' in 'bwytais i frecwast'.

target: Dylai fe gael mwy o gwsg.
english: He should get more sleep.
tip: 'dylai' means should or ought to, so 'dylai fe' is he should. Its verb-noun soft-mutates: 'cael' becomes 'gael'.

target: Os daw e, bydda i'n hapus.
english: If he comes, I'll be happy.
tip: 'os' (if) for a real condition takes the future. 'daw' means he'll come, the irregular future of 'dod' (to come).

target: Mae'r siocled tywyll yn cynnwys siwgr llai.
english: The dark chocolate contains less sugar.
tip: 'llai' means less or fewer and is irregular, not built with '-ach'. Here 'siwgr llai' is less sugar.

target: Gwelodd Dylan y trên yn gadael yr orsaf.
english: Dylan saw the train leaving the station.
tip: A feminine noun normally soft-mutates after the article 'y' or 'yr': 'gorsaf' (station) becomes 'yr orsaf'.

target: Roedd angen mwy o amser arnon ni i orffen y prosiect.
english: We needed more time to finish the project.
tip: Need uses 'angen' plus 'ar', so the need sits on the person. 'arnon ni' means on us, so we needed it.

target: Pe bawn i'n siarad mwy o Gymraeg, byddwn i'n teimlo'n fwy hyderus.
english: If I spoke more Welsh, I'd feel more confident.
tip: 'pe' is if for an unreal condition: 'pe bawn i' means if I were, and 'byddwn i' is I would.

target: Mae hi'n dalach na'i brawd.
english: She is taller than her brother.
tip: Short adjectives usually add '-ach' for the comparative: 'tal' (tall) becomes 'talach', shown here as 'dalach' after 'yn'.

target: Er mwyn cael gwell swydd.
english: In order to get a better job.
tip: 'er mwyn' plus a verb-noun means in order to: 'er mwyn cael' is in order to get.

target: Mae fy chwaer yn iau na fi.
english: My sister is younger than me.
tip: 'iau' (younger) is the irregular comparative of 'ifanc' (young), not 'ifancach'. Than is 'na'.

target: Gorffennodd hi'r ras mewn llai nag awr.
english: She finished the race in under an hour.
tip: Than is 'nag' before a vowel and 'na' before a consonant. 'awr' starts with a vowel, so 'llai nag awr'.

target: Gorau po gyntaf y byddwch chi'n dechrau.
english: The sooner you start, the better.
tip: 'po' plus a superlative builds the more or the -er: 'gorau po gyntaf' means the sooner, the better.

target: Dyma'r llwybr mwyaf poblogaidd o bell ffordd.
english: This is by far the most popular trail.
tip: Longer adjectives take 'mwyaf' (most) in front for the superlative: 'mwyaf poblogaidd' is most popular.

target: Fy mam sy'n gwneud y cawl gorau.
english: It's my mother who makes the best cawl.
tip: Front the subject and follow it with 'sy'n' to say it is X who: 'fy mam sy'n' means it's my mum who.

target: Mae Sioned yn fwy parod na fi i siarad Cymraeg.
english: Sioned is more willing than me to speak Welsh.
tip: Longer adjectives use 'yn fwy' plus adjective plus 'na' for more...than: 'yn fwy parod na fi', more willing than me.

target: Mae'r bws cynharach yn aml yn llai llawn.
english: The earlier bus is often less crowded.
tip: Use 'yn llai' plus an adjective for less...: 'yn llai llawn' means less full.

target: Ar ôl i'r storm basio, ymddangosodd enfys hardd.
english: After the storm passed, a beautiful rainbow appeared.
tip: 'ar ôl i' plus a subject plus a verb-noun means after X did; the verb soft-mutates, so 'pasio' becomes 'basio'.

target: Y peth pwysicaf yw bod pawb yn iach.
english: The most important thing is that everyone is healthy.
tip: Most superlatives end in '-af': 'pwysig' (important) becomes 'pwysicaf', the most important.

target: Mae angen mwy o gyllid ar wasanaethau iechyd meddwl.
english: Mental health services need more funding.
tip: The word 'o' (of) triggers soft mutation: 'cyllid' (funding) becomes 'mwy o gyllid', more funding.

target: Mae Llundain yn fwy na Chaerdydd.
english: London is bigger than Cardiff.
tip: The word 'na' (than) triggers aspirate mutation, so 'Caerdydd' becomes 'na Chaerdydd'.

target: Mae'r Gymraeg yn hŷn na'r Saesneg.
english: Welsh is older than English.
tip: 'hŷn' (older) is the irregular comparative of 'hen' (old), not 'henach'. Than is 'na'.

target: Mae e-lyfrau ar gael.
english: E-books are available.
tip: 'ar gael' is a set phrase meaning available, built from 'cael' (to get): 'mae e-lyfrau ar gael', e-books are available.

target: Mae e'n fwy defnyddiol.
english: It's more useful.
tip: Linking 'yn' softens the adjective: 'mwy' becomes 'fwy'. 'yn fwy' plus an adjective means more, as in 'fwy defnyddiol'.

target: Dw i'n cytuno â'r athro.
english: I agree with the teacher.
tip: 'cytuno' takes 'â' for with, never 'gyda': 'cytuno â'r athro', agree with the teacher.

target: Dw i'n gweithio tuag at ddyrchafiad.
english: I'm working towards a promotion.
tip: 'tuag at' means towards and softens what follows: 'dyrchafiad' becomes 'ddyrchafiad'.

target: Dylai mwy o bobl ddysgu Cymraeg.
english: More people should learn Welsh.
tip: 'dylai' means should: 'dylai mwy o bobl ddysgu Cymraeg', more people should learn Welsh.

target: Llai yw mwy o ran sesnin.
english: Less is more when it comes to seasoning.
tip: 'llai' is the irregular word for less, from 'bach' (small). It never takes an '-ach' ending.

target: Dyw hi ddim yn gallu mynychu'r seremoni.
english: She can't attend the ceremony.
tip: Negate the present with 'dyw' ... 'ddim': 'dyw hi ddim yn gallu', she can't.
